summary.text: Jocelyn Benson is Michigan's 43rd Secretary of State and the Democratic nominee for governor, with running mate Winnie Brinks. A former Wayne State University law dean, she was elected secretary of state in 2018 and re-elected in 2022. Her campaign emphasizes housing, health-care costs, child care and education, and she has said she would pass gun-safety legislation.

paragraphs.text: Benson was raised in Pittsburgh. She earned a B.A. from Wellesley College, a master's degree as a Marshall Scholar at Oxford, and a J.D. from Harvard Law School.

She began teaching at Wayne State University Law School in 2005. In 2012, at age 36, she was appointed its dean, a post she held until 2016; the Department of State says she was then the youngest woman in U.S. history to lead a top-100, accredited law school.
She founded the school's Levin Center with former U.S. Sen. Carl Levin and continues as vice chair of its advisory board.
From 2016 to 2018 she led the Ross Initiative in Sports for Equality.
Benson lost her first race for secretary of state, in 2010. She won the office in 2018, and was re-elected in 2022.
